questionText:
Let $S$ be the following schedule of operations of three transactions $T_1, T_2$ and $T_3$ in a relational database system:

$$R_2(Y), R_1(X), R_3(Z), R_1(Y), W_1(X), R_2(Z), W_2(Y), R_3(X), W_3(Z)$$

Consider the statements $P$ and $Q$ below:

P: $S$ is conflict-serializable.
Q: If $T_3$ commits before $T_1$ finishes, then $S$ is recoverable.

Which one of the following choices is correct?
options: Both P and Q are true.
P is true and Q is false.
P is false and Q is true.
Both P and Q are false.
explanation:
1. Checking Statement P:
To test for conflict serializability, construct the precedence graph (serialization graph) by examining conflicting operations on the same data item:
• Data item X: $W_1(X)$ precedes $R_3(X) \implies$ Edge $T_1 \rightarrow T_3$
• Data item Y: $R_1(Y)$ precedes $W_2(Y) \implies$ Edge $T_1 \rightarrow T_2$
• Data item Z: $R_2(Z)$ precedes $W_3(Z) \implies$ Edge $T_2 \rightarrow T_3$

The edges in the precedence graph are $T_1 \rightarrow T_2$, $T_1 \rightarrow T_3$, and $T_2 \rightarrow T_3$. Since there are no cycles (topological ordering: $T_1, T_2, T_3$), the schedule $S$ is conflict-serializable.
Therefore, P is true.

2. Checking Statement Q:
A schedule is recoverable if any transaction $T_j$ that reads data written by transaction $T_i$ commits only after $T_i$ commits.
In schedule $S$, transaction $T_3$ reads $X$ written by $T_1$ ($W_1(X)$ occurs before $R_3(X)$).
For $S$ to be recoverable, $T_1$ must commit before $T_3$ commits.
If $T_3$ commits before $T_1$ finishes (commits), $S$ is unrecoverable.
Therefore, Q is false.

Hence, P is true and Q is false.
